metrics.label: Stored tensor elements
metrics.explanation: Includes stored buffers and quantization scales; not a trainable-parameter count.

metrics.label: Active parameters per token
metrics.explanation: Dense-model approximation using stored tensor elements, including any buffers.

metrics.label: Model structure
metrics.explanation: Read from supported model geometry; other pipelines may contain multiple components.

metrics.label: Weight storage footprint
metrics.explanation: Tensor elements × storage bytes. This is a floor: the runtime may expand BF16 or quantized weights, especially on CPU.
metrics.formula: Sum of bytes across each published tensor dtype

metrics.label: Attention cache per token
metrics.explanation: Key and value × layers × KV heads × head width × bytes per element
metrics.formula: Key and value × layers × KV heads × head width × bytes per element

metrics.label: Attention cache, before sharding
metrics.explanation: 4,096 cached tokens × 1 simultaneous sequences; BF16 cache.
metrics.formula: Cache bytes per token × cached tokens × concurrent sequences

metrics.label: Runtime allowance
metrics.explanation: 15% for activations, workspaces and runtime. Validate observed peak memory.

metrics.label: Memory before parallelism
metrics.explanation: One logical model copy; the GPU layout below includes replicated cache.

metrics.label: BF16 tensors
metrics.explanation: 7,615,616,512 stored elements × 2 bytes per element.

metrics.label: Requests in this period
metrics.explanation: Tokens alone do not establish a request count.

metrics.label: Input volume
metrics.explanation: The input portion of the declared traffic.

metrics.label: Output volume
metrics.explanation: The generated portion of the declared traffic.

metrics.label: Average input demand
metrics.explanation: Average over the complete comparison period.

metrics.label: Average output demand
metrics.explanation: Average demand does not describe bursts.

metrics.label: Decode-equivalent peak demand
metrics.explanation: A planning normalization that depends on the supplied prefill ratio and peak multiplier.
metrics.formula: (Output/s + input/s ÷ prefill speed ratio) × peak multiplier

metrics.label: Node profile
metrics.explanation: A hardware planning profile; Region availability, quota and capacity have not been checked.

metrics.label: Accelerator
metrics.explanation: 1 GPUs per node.

metrics.label: Published GPU memory per node
metrics.explanation: Uses the EC2 specification's binary units, not a marketing GB label.

metrics.label: GPUs sharing one model copy
metrics.explanation: Memory and attention-head divisibility fit this planning profile. The serving engine still needs validation.
metrics.formula: Smallest supported degree in 1, 2, 4, 8 that divides attention heads and fits memory

metrics.label: Memory across this model copy
metrics.explanation: Includes repeated cache where the attention layout requires it.
metrics.formula: (Weights per GPU + cache per GPU) × (1 + allowance) × GPUs

metrics.label: Memory required on each GPU
metrics.explanation: The per-GPU limit must pass; aggregate memory alone is insufficient.

metrics.label: Within-node connection
metrics.explanation: No inter-node tensor parallelism is modeled.

metrics.label: Maximum copies by GPU count
metrics.explanation: A density limit only. Shared-node contention and memory must be tested.

metrics.label: Idealized decode ceiling
metrics.explanation: Analytical roofline using dense BF16 compute and memory bandwidth. This is not measured throughput.
metrics.formula: Min(compute ÷ (2 × active parameters), bandwidth × batch ÷ bytes read per decode step)

metrics.label: Traffic-based replica floor
metrics.explanation: One replica per node for fault isolation. Requires a prefill ratio; final capacity needs a load test.
metrics.formula: Max(availability floor, ceil(peak demand ÷ (decode ceiling × utilization)))

metrics.label: Nodes at that planning floor
metrics.explanation: Copies are spread across nodes. Placement across Availability Zones is not established.

metrics.label: Hourly node rate
metrics.explanation: Linux shared-tenancy EC2 On-Demand. SageMaker Hosting and commitment rates are separate.

metrics.label: One node over this period
metrics.explanation: 720 hours. Compute only; storage, networking and other charges are additional.

metrics.label: Fleet compute at the planning floor
metrics.explanation: An estimate for the modeled replica floor. It is not the hosting comparison's recommendation.

metrics.label: First-token latency
metrics.explanation: Requires a streaming benchmark for this model, engine, workload and GPU layout.

guidance.title: Establish the workload before choosing compute
guidance.reason: CPU versus GPU depends on the runtime, deadline, memory and arrival rate. A model size or traffic total alone cannot answer it.

checks.label: CPU runtime
checks.detail: Confirm all operators and dependencies run on CPU. A laptop with no discrete GPU may still use Apple Metal or another integrated accelerator.

checks.label: Delivery
checks.detail: Include queueing, image pull, model loading and generation in a batch deadline.

checks.label: Concurrent jobs
checks.detail: Low concurrency is an experiment priority, not a proof that CPU will meet demand.

checks.label: Completion budget
checks.detail: A batch completion budget differs from first-token or first-audio latency.

checks.label: CPU memory screen
checks.detail: The selected CPU profile has 64 GiB RAM. Include every loaded model, decoder, process and concurrent worker; a weight-only estimate is a floor.

cpuServices.name: AWS Batch
cpuServices.detail: Run a container on EC2 CPU instances or Fargate. Start with a job deadline, queue limits and a scale-down policy. Startup and model loading count toward the deadline.

cpuServices.name: Amazon ECS on Fargate
cpuServices.detail: Use for compatible CPU jobs or services within the supported task sizes. Include image pull and model download. Fargate does not expose GPUs.

cpuServices.name: Amazon EC2 CPU
cpuServices.fit: Control over memory, instructions and model reuse
cpuServices.detail: Compare compute-optimized C instances and memory-optimized R instances using measured process memory. Persistent workers can amortize loading; allocated instances cost money while idle.

cpuServices.name: Amazon SageMaker AI CPU
cpuServices.detail: CPU endpoints and Batch Transform can serve compatible models. Check the container, payload limits, job mode and instance support. SageMaker does not imply GPU.

cpuServices.name: AWS Lambda
cpuServices.detail: For standard Lambda functions, test the 10,240 MB memory and 15-minute invocation limits, package size, cold starts and available CPU. A model that fits on disk may still exceed process memory. Evaluate other Lambda compute modes separately.

sizeGuidance: There is no universal parameter-count cutoff. Measure peak resident memory, supported operations and time per item.
A rough weight-only floor is parameters × bytes per parameter: FP32 uses 4, BF16/FP16 2, INT8 1. Runtime expansion, caches, audio decoders and simultaneous models add memory.

For scale: 1.7B FP32 weights alone need about 6.3 GiB; 7B need 26.1 GiB; 70B need 260.8 GiB. Halving storage precision only halves that floor if the CPU runtime actually uses it without expanding the weights.
Large generative models, long context, high concurrency or a missed deadline can make CPU impractical even when RAM is sufficient.
guidance.graviton: Graviton is an ARM CPU option, not a GPU. Build an ARM64 image with compatible libraries and kernels, then compare completed work per dollar against x86. Do not reuse an x86 timing or assume a fixed speedup.

example.title: A podcast generated on CPU
example.description: One recorded AWS Batch run produced a four-turn, two-voice sample. This is an example from the application owner's experiment, not a benchmark of your project.
limitations: One short run does not establish a percentile, production throughput, a full-episode deadline or performance on Graviton.
Generation was slower than playback. This run does not demonstrate real-time voice.
Two model variants and audio components were loaded. A parameter count alone would understate process memory.
Voice quality requires listening tests. No controlled comparison against another speech service was recorded.
No AWS access, security approval, deployment recipe or current price is established by this example.
